positions.locationName: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

positions.title: Piano Accompanist
positions.description: • Provided accompaniment for students, soloists, and choruses in various competitions and community performances.

positions.title: Security Data Engineer
positions.description:
• Designed and developed internal tools to optimize the web security incident response process, boosting overall output and efficacy by more than 50%.
• Performed data classification, sanitation and aggregation on ground truth data powering Cisco’s web & email security solutions.
• Built data pipelines and visualizations to assess team performance and key product metrics.
• Interfaced with global tier 1 customer support to triage and resolve customer complaints and technical issues.

positions.title: Electronics Engineer
positions.description:
• Performed investigative work (parts research, consumer follow-up, statistical analysis) on ongoing vehicle control safety defects investigations.
• Developed software solutions that enable investigators to efficiently aggregate and analyze vehicle owner questionnaires (VOQ).
• Developed and maintained a knowledge base of recent vehicle cybersecurity research activities among public/private sectors internationally.
• Investigated the possible correlation between a vehicle's internal network architecture and vulnerability to cyber-attacks; developed a general approach to convert electrical schematics in service manuals into high-level system diagrams, which provide at-a-glance views to the connections between safety modules and remote attack surfaces.
• Researched the administrative and technical causes of various high-profile automotive incidents in recent years, including the Toyota unintended acceleration incident and the GM ignition switch incident; assessed the perspectives of government agencies, OEMs, private sector experts, consumers, and the general public on these incidents.
• Attended the TRB 94th Annual Meeting and the SAE Government/Industry Meeting 2015 to understand the current research & development in autonomous vehicles and cybersecurity of automotive systems.

company.name: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), US Department of Transportation

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Designed and produced simulation modules using LabVIEW to collect real time pressure levels of various ultra-high vacuum (UHV) chambers, which enabled monitoring and analysis of pressure fluctuations and trends.
• Researched and recommended procedures to perform hydrogen cracking and semiconductor surface oxide removal in UHV, after surface oxide pollution was found on a laboratory equipment.
• Designed and produced computer-aided design (CAD) drawings for a transport arm supporting relocation of laboratory equipment while maintaining UHV environment. The design received approval from supervisors and the team is currently undergoing assembly of the final product.
• Configured and maintained the laboratory's transport arm control system (via Aerotech Soloist) and GPIB network.

company.name: Institute of Research in Electronics and Applied Physics (IREAP), University of Maryland

volunteerExperiences.description:
• Regularly develop and lead Sunday school lessons for K-6 children.
• Regularly provide preludes, postludes, and worship hymns for Sunday services. 
• Regularly serve in the praise band to lead worship sessions during Sunday services.
• Co-organized annual Vacation Bible Schools (VBS), which are full-day, week-long summer camps for K-6 children. Wrote and directed four 10-minute long skits for youth to perform each year, in addition to many other interactive activities and logistical groundwork.

• Joined the Leadership and Community Service-Learning (LCSL) program of University of Maryland.
• Committed to weekly tutoring service at the Math Heroes program and bi-weekly community dialogues to understand and act against present social issues.

projects.title: Bikeshare Intended Keyless Encrypted Smartlocks (BIKES)
projects.description:
• Team BIKES is an undergraduate research team under the Gemstone Honors Program at the University of Maryland, College Park. Team BIKES seeks to develop a proof of concept of a novel bikeshare model tailored to college campuses.
• Researched and proposed possible methods to wirelessly transfer locational data of individual bicycles to computers and mobile devices. The results were included in the “geolocation” section of the research proposal, which was reviewed and approved by a board of researchers and experts.
• Digitally created visual aids and animations to aid clarification of specialized concepts and complex systems on team presentations.
